## 2026-10-14 — I493 worker administrator authority, and the 10.0.101 toolchain

The pinned 10.0.401 SDK is no longer installed on the build host, so at the owner's instruction `global.json` now selects the installed **10.0.101**. That SDK bundles .NET 10.0.1 packs, so `Directory.Build.targets` pins the runtime, apphost and crossgen packs to the serviced **10.0.13** security release: a self-contained publish bundles 10.0.13 (`System.Private.CoreLib` 10.0.13-servicing, `coreclr` 10,0,1326,50504) and its `runtimeconfig.json` names 10.0.13, instead of silently shipping a ten-month-old runtime. Framework-dependent builds keep rolling forward at run time. The whole solution builds with zero errors.

Exact parent `3d338fc9` then proved a containment defect: `RestrictedProcess.LowIntegrityToken` lowered only the integrity label of a duplicate of FileCat's own token, so an elevated FileCat handed the worker that parses hostile input an **enabled `BUILTIN\Administrators` SID and all 24 administrator privileges**. Low integrity restricts writes, not reads; Windows' own `AccessCheck` granted that token `FILE_GENERIC_READ` on an administrators-only file, and a started worker returned its contents. The worker token is now taken from the session's UAC-filtered token where Windows offers one, restricted with `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE` and with every privileged group it carries made deny-only, lowered to low integrity and **verified before use**; a token that still holds administrative authority is refused, and `CanUseFallbackToken` already denies an elevated parent the ordinary fallback, so no unrestricted worker starts in its place. The job object also sets `JOB_OBJECT_UILIMIT_HANDLES`, denying the worker FileCat's own USER handles.

Four controls change from 0P/4F to 4P/0F with only `FileCat.Platform.Windows.dll` replaced (parent `bf9ac3df`, fixed `c34e1f83`, test assembly `44023344`), the parent DLL built from a separate detached worktree so the shared checkout stayed untouched. The elevated host passes **14P/0F/0S**, the VM's signed-in medium session **14P/0F/4 elevated-only skips**, and an elevated run inside that signed-in session (scheduled task, interactive principal, highest run level) **14P/0F/0S**. The full host Platform suite is **439 total/5 failed/35 skips**, and all five failures reproduce at the exact parent, so they predate this slice and are kept for separate triage; `FileCat.Core.Tests` passes **4,256P/0F/141S**.

The tests' former `cmd.exe` stand-in exits `0xC0000142` under the restricted token wherever the session's own token carries no logon SID, because a console program needs a console and that needs window-station access: the measured WinSta0 DACL grants its full rights to the console logon SID and to Administrators, and the `Default` desktop DACL has no ACE for the plain user SID. FileCat's real helpers are `WinExe` and started normally in every session, so the tests now use the new windowless `FileCat.WorkerProbe`, matching what the product starts. Nine-file private archive `i493-worker-authority-20261014-v1`, manifest SHA-256 `6d62e6f76e986ae64ac0dbb29d7d40f408694de99f52e82d358e6c2b3fa8140c`; details in [E-I493](evidence/E-I493-worker-administrator-authority.md). The Windows VM was reverted to its `updated #38` snapshot at the owner's instruction before these VM runs. No candidate, publication or human GO follows, and the I106/I110 physical-source hold is untouched.

## 2026-10-14 — I494 Unix worker root identity, and a green local Windows suite

The Windows worker fix has a Unix counterpart. FileCat may be started with root rights because a recovery session reads devices directly, and `PictureWorker` then handed every picture to a decoder running as uid 0: the seccomp filter it applies denies `fork`/`vfork`/`execve`/`execveat`/`clone3` and sets `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`, which bounds what the worker may start and nothing about what it may read or rewrite, with SkiaSharp's native codecs as the parsing surface. macOS had no filter at all.

`UnixWorkerIdentity.Drop` now runs before the worker reads a byte: supplementary groups, then group, then user, to the account sudo records as the requester, verified down to `setuid(0)` no longer succeeding; a worker that is root with no requesting user decodes nothing and returns the reason. On the owned Ubuntu 26.04 VM, with the worker probe calling the product's own code against a `600` `root:root` sentinel file: an ordinary user is unchanged and refused the file, root through sudo becomes **0:0 → 1000:1000** irreversibly and is refused the file, and root with `SUDO_UID` cleared refuses to decode while the probe shows that same authority reading the sentinel. Two host controls cover the ordinary-user and Windows paths. The macOS root case uses the same code but is **not verified**: that machine's account needs a sudo password this campaign does not hold. Five-file archive `i494-unix-worker-root-20261014-v1`, manifest `0456a64f8e9df997d1eb0c087a181748af2bdd424fd9adb8a8d22512004a7b1d`; see [E-I494](evidence/E-I494-unix-worker-root-identity.md).

Separately, the five Windows Platform failures standing on the development host were traced to the tests, not the product: they put fixtures wherever the temporary folder lives, and this computer refuses direct reads of its system volume — `\\.\C:` answers ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED at offset 0 for plain `CreateFile`/`ReadFile` as well, while `\\.\E:`, `\\.\G:` and `\\.\PhysicalDrive3` all return a `55 AA` boot sector. The four administrator record tests and the elevated volume-read test now take their fixture root from the first NTFS volume whose raw sectors this computer actually allows FileCat to read, prefer the temporary folder's own volume, and skip with the system's own refusal message when no volume allows it (`FILECAT_RAW_FIXTURE_ROOT` overrides). With that, the local suites are green for the first time in this campaign: Platform **439P/0F/35S**, Core **4,256P/0F/141S**, App **1,689P/0F/42S**.

## 2026-10-15 — I495 physical source attribution, zero-write proof and a served-length correction

The owner reconfirmed the disposable USB stick and authorized destructive use. Two full device images with per-chunk hashes were taken around FileCat's own read-only recovery tests on the mounted NTFS volume, and the whole-device hash changed again, as in [G6](evidence/E-V09-G6-incomplete-usb-source-trace.md). This time it is located and identified: **4 of 1,859 chunks, 64 of 15,224 sectors, 32,768 bytes of 7.8 GB**, and every changed sector is file-system metadata — `RSTR`/`RCRD` journal records in the 16 MiB before the MFT zone, `FILE` records at the volume's own `Mft Start Lcn` (`0xC0000`), `INDX` directory index blocks and the `$MFTMirr` area. No user-data region differs.

The attribution is then closed from both sides. Statically, every device open in the recovery paths asks for read access only and all seven IOCTLs it issues are queries; there is no write handle, lock, dismount or flush of a source anywhere in them. Dynamically, the same scans were repeated with the disk made read-only at the storage layer (a write attempt is refused with `IOException` while the volume stays mounted): the device hash is `a9c5d4bab25cea3488bb1def137c42ee9222713ec67215c9ef58c040f6b09c14` before, after the first run and after a second run — **byte-identical, so FileCat changed none of the 7,796,162,560 bytes**, while both scans reported the same 326 deleted files (126 Overwritten, 1 Partial, 199 Recoverable). The stick was returned to read/write and verified writable.

The strict physical comparison also caught the [I110](FILECAT_1_0_RELEASE_ISSUES.md#i110) risk for real: the direct and helper paths both returned **904 of the last 5,000 bytes** of the volume and compared equal. The volume device serves nothing from its final 4,096 bytes — `IOCTL_DISK_GET_LENGTH_INFO` reports the partition's 7,795,113,984 while reads stop at 7,795,109,888, exactly the file system's own size of 1,903,103 clusters — and plain `CreateFile`/`ReadFile` behave identically, while `\\.\PhysicalDrive5` serves those bytes, so the NTFS backup boot sector is reachable only from the whole disk. `DeviceTopology.ServedLength` now reports what a device will serve, for the direct source and the installed helper alike; the on-stick comparison then reads the full 5,000 bytes through both paths with identical hashes. A new live control covers the lost-partition path on real hardware: scanning `\\.\PhysicalDrive5` read-only finds `NTFS at 1048576 (7434 MiB)` identically through the helper protocol and directly.

CI caught one consequence of the earlier toolchain slice: publishing refuses a runtime pack whose license texts are not pinned and reviewed in `licenses/dependencies`, which is the case for 10.0.13, so the serviced pin moves to the reviewed **10.0.12** and the notice gate passes locally (50 verified files). The remaining Windows CI failures in both runs are timeouts scattered across unrelated Core, App and Remote suites, different tests each run; the three Windows App cases from the first run pass locally in Release in eight seconds, so they are recorded as the known hosted-runner timing class rather than a regression. Twenty-four-file archive `i495-usb-source-safety-20261014-v1`, manifest `67f0268557bcaea9f2495f7adbdadfaf2956f5fc07c2e829420430ca9f550da2`, keeps both images so a future difference can be read back. Details in [E-I495](evidence/E-I495-usb-source-write-attribution.md). The signed-program fixture, destructive ground-truth scenarios, consent paths, other media and the candidate remain; no publication or human GO follows.

## 2026-10-15 — the destructive recovery ground truth passes on real hardware

With the source-write question answered, the owner's destructive authorization was used for the gate it exists for. `LiveDriveScenarioTests` formats the authorized stick, writes generated files, has Windows delete most of them, scans through the helper's read protocol and compares every byte FileCat calls recovered with what was written. **All three file systems pass, 432 s in total**: FAT32 finds 328 of 328 written items and reads back 74 MiB (327 Recoverable, one Overwritten with its missing range named), exFAT the same at a 32,768-byte cluster size, and NTFS 326 of 328 with 71 MiB read back, all Recoverable. The fixture deliberately contains a file whose data is gone, a fragmented file and an overwritten one, and none of the unrecoverable ones is offered as recoverable.

A bound was then added to the new served-length probe: a damaged source answers a refused read slowly, so the end is probed at most sixteen times instead of searching 64 KiB down a failing device. Two unit controls state that contract — a few reserved sectors are trimmed, an implausible overstatement is left as the device reported it — and the full Windows Platform suite passes **444 tests with 36 explicit skips**. The live USB suite is then green end to end. The stick, freshly formatted by the destructive gate, received 40 signed Windows programs (18.0 MiB) which Windows then deleted, and `LiveDriveRecoveryTests` passes **5 of 5 with no skips**: both the quick and the free-space scan find 326 deleted files, recover all 40 programs in 0.6 s, and the recovered signatures verify **7 valid, 33 unsigned, none altered** — the 33 being catalog-signed system libraries that an embedded-signature check reports as unsigned, as earlier runs recorded. ## 2026-10-15 — I496 helper description, page refusals in the real engines, a hostile ZIP, and a long fuzz campaign

Four slices, continuing the autonomous queue after the physical-source work.

**[I496](evidence/E-I496-helper-drive-description.md).** A recovery session asks the administrator helper one `Info` question and took the answer as given: `PipeDeviceSource` stored the reported length and sector size unchecked, although nothing else in the session can corroborate that answer and the length becomes the scan's bounds, `WindowSource`'s bounds and the progress arithmetic. A fake helper over a real named pipe shows seven descriptions all accepted — length `0`, `-1` and `long.MaxValue`, sector sizes `0`, `-4096`, `3` and 1 MiB. The description is now refused where it arrives: a positive length no larger than a pebibyte and a sector size that is a power of two between 512 bytes and 64 KiB. `BrokeredDeviceSource` inherits that constructor, so the installed-helper path is covered too. Eight controls, seven failing before the fix.

**[I25 page refusals](evidence/E-I25-page-web-refusals.md).** The page view's policy was implemented and described; it is now measured in the real engines. A local page asking the web for a stylesheet, a web font, a frame, an image and its own next page has all four resources refused by host and the navigation cancelled (`OperationCanceled`), keeping its own title; a page that sends itself a download — the only way left with scripts off — has it cancelled (`ConnectionAborted`) with nothing written to any Downloads folder. Both pass on the development host with the installed WebView2 155.0.4283.45 and on the disposable VM in its signed-in and elevated sessions, where the whole set of this stretch's controls runs **22P/0F** (four elevated-only skips at medium integrity, none elevated). The macOS smoke tool passes at this commit on the owner's Mac over SSH: the page keeps its own title so its script did not run, one remote request is refused, the Markdown page asks the web for nothing, and 12 of 12 engine lifecycles end with no event after disposal. Popups and permission prompts stay code-level, because with scripts off neither can be reached without a human click.

**A hostile ZIP.** The TAR escape case was covered end to end; ZIP, the format people actually receive, was not. A ZIP carrying `../escape-up.txt`, `..\escape-win.txt`, `deep/../../escape-deep.txt`, `/abs-root.txt`, `C:/abs-drive.txt`, `host.txt:stream` and `./dot-prefixed.txt` is extracted beside one ordinary member, and both guards fire: the provider refuses the climbing and absolute names as they are read, and the name check refuses the two `':'` members as they would be written. Only `ok/inner.txt` lands; nothing appears beside the destination, in the temporary folder or at the drive root; no `host.txt` and no alternate data stream exist; every file under the destination resolves inside it.

**[A long fuzz campaign](evidence/E-FUZZ-long-campaign-20261015.md).** The four damage harnesses ran far past their defaults with **no failure**: recovery 30,000 rounds on each of seven images (210,000 damaged-image scans, 150× its default), inspector 30,000 per format, archive 2,000 per format and discovery 50,000, with the retained I28/I37 rounds still passing. The archive harness writes real archives and is I/O-bound: a 15,000-round attempt ran over an hour without finishing and was stopped in favour of the completed run. Seven-file archive `fuzz-campaign-20261015-v1`, manifest `05b884939c2a138ceed53f1bd96e8937cfe42a0f63a8e71c9f2e41a015486d94`.

**Audited and found sound, so nothing changed:** the elevation plan validator (nonce, freshness window, requesting SID, the device-path and session-name patterns, Registry/file field mixing, whole-volume protections, same-volume moves); the Shell helper's answers (1,024-pixel cap, bounded message, no overflow in the 4 MiB worst case); the update check's URL (https, default port, `github.com`, no user info, path under the project's releases, otherwise the hard-coded page); SSH known-hosts and FTPS certificate handling (no blanket accept, described prompts, revoked and changed keys distinguished); every `Process.Start` site (the two shell-execute paths are explicit user actions); and Unix device sizing (sector size bounded, non-positive lengths refused, a Linux partition serving its whole extent). The ZIP listing shows a hostile member under its sanitized name while extraction refuses it, which keeps such a member viewable; that is deliberately unlike the stricter archive provider and was left alone.

Local suites at this commit: Platform **454P/36S**, Remote **2,526P/156S**, Core **4,259P/142S**, App **1,689P/42S**, no failures. The three CI runs after the runtime-notice correction (`1c225975`, `2f6d432c`, `a7df8dfd`) are green on all five required jobs, so the earlier Windows timeouts did not recur and the ARM64 notice failure is gone. ## 2026-10-29 — SharpCompress shipped OSI-only; 7z members checked (I14 remediated preliminarily)

The second half of the EXT-02 route is done ([record](evidence/E-I14-sharpcompress-osi.md)). FileCat ships SharpCompress as its own build (`FileCat.SharpCompress.dll`), cut down to what FileCat reads with it: 7z, bzip2, xz and zstd.
- **What went.** The UnRAR-derived RAR and PPMd var.H code, and every other format, writer and codec. Among them are the Info-ZIP-licensed Implode and Reduce decoders, and the codecs whose terms were not established. DotNetZip's CRC32 class, credited to vbAccelerator, is replaced.
- **Licenses.** The assembly declares `MIT AND Apache-2.0 AND MS-PL AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause AND Zlib`, all OSI-approved. RAR 3 and 7z PPMd share FileCat's rardecode-derived model.
- **A real defect found and fixed.** SharpCompress never checked a 7z member's CRC-32 on the stream FileCat reads, so a damaged 7z could read back as wrong bytes. FileCat now refuses such members. Over 300 single-bit damages per coder, none reads as if whole.
- **Verification.** A zero-warning build; the Core suite (4,937 tests, 0 failed); 16,000 archive fuzz rounds; all validators. Packages were built from the clean commit on Windows, Ubuntu 24.04.5 and macOS 27, and each carries the pinned license set and an SBOM with the expression.

## 2026-10-29 — Recheck of Codex's `f134ba37`; archive readers bounded (I557–I559) and R-H5 fixed

**The recheck** ([record](evidence/E-REVIEW-2026-10-29-f134ba37.md)). Three independent read-only reviews covered the security plan's AC-15–44 execution: 44 product files and their tests. Many corrections hold: the AC-15, AC-31 and AC-33 handle protocols, the high-integrity refusals, and the SFV, FAT and NTFS parsers. Nine High findings remain:
- **Renames on Linux and macOS.** A case-only rename on a case-insensitive volume is refused; on the Ubuntu VM's FAT32, where the old code silently left the name unchanged, it now says the name already exists. Every rename on NFS or FUSE without `rename2` fails.
- **Replace.** It fails over 64 MiB on Windows fixed drives, with a false message, and on removable drives, and every refusal comes after the whole copy. The owner accepted the Linux/macOS/UNC/link refusal as policy (`2b62355f`).
- **Reparse points.** Every one counts as a link, OneDrive placeholder folders included.
- **SUBST drives.** A path on one resolves to a sibling folder for permanent delete; the resolution was observed on this host, and nothing was deleted.
- **Amplification.** Registry import preview and Markdown (tables and quadratic patterns).
- **AC-20.** A mount-point route around it is plausible.
- **macOS temporary folders** below `/var`, a symbolic link, are refused. Hosted macOS fails 42 tests for it, and a test hangs on the Mac.

There are also six Medium and seven Low, and tests changed to expect less. R-H1, R-M1–R-M3, R-M9 and R-M14 are still open. **Since `f134ba37` hosted CI fails on every platform lane:** macOS fails 42 tests and is cancelled, Ubuntu fails two OpenPGP helper tests, Windows x64 is cancelled and ARM64 fails. All of this is the security session's to fix.

**Fixed by the release session** ([record](evidence/E-I557-archive-pass-budget.md)), in its own archive readers, SharpCompress build and RAR reader:
- **I557, High.** To open a 7z member, every earlier entry was decoded without a limit, even in another folder. A compressed TAR decompressed a whole member before its 1000:1 check, and cancellation could not stop it. A 1,710-byte tar.bz2 decoded 2 GiB just to list.
- **I558, High.** A 7z member read only in part shifted the next member of its folder, so a healthy solid 7z was reported damaged. Before the CRC check of `34bc2abb`, it read back as wrong bytes.
- **R-H5.** A packed 7z header was allocated at its claimed size: 200 MiB from a 70-byte file.
- **I559, High.** Codex's RAR-SEC-001 correction `a718c777` capped a solid RAR's run at 8 GiB. A healthy solid RAR with an 8.5 GiB member could not be read past it, not even in archive order.

`3a63099e`, `98bb2ce1` and `3bb3d995` fix them:
- In the 7z reader, only entries in the member's own folder are decoded to pass, under 1000 times the archive's size, and the handed-out entry is finished first.
- The TAR stream checks every read and observes cancellation.
- A packed header's buffer grows only as it decodes, up to 256 MiB.
- A solid RAR's run is bounded by its expansion ratio alone; the 8.5 GiB archive now reads through.

Six of the eleven new tests fail on the old code. The full Core suite passes on Windows, and the archive classes on Ubuntu.

**Ledger.**
- Issues are now **559/538/2/19**, and the evidence index **897**.
- REL-REVIEW-CODEX-20261029 stays Open for the security session's findings.

Stable publication remains NO-GO.

## 2026-10-29 — The `f134ba37` recheck's nine High fixed; what still broke hosted CI fixed (I560, I561)

**At the owner's instruction**, the release session took over the nine High findings ([record](evidence/E-REVIEW-2026-10-29-f134ba37.md#high-findings-fixed-by-the-release-session)). Two subagents in their own worktrees took Registry and Markdown; the security session meanwhile wrote a new review pass into its plan and changed no product file.
- **F-H1 (`505cf1bb`).** A case-only rename on a volume that ignores case goes through a temporary name. Without rename flags (NFS, 9p, FUSE), a file's new name is claimed with a hard link, which never replaces.
- **F-H2 (`4f6743e1`).** A destination over the 64 MiB review budget, or kept by a cloud provider, is replaced by identity, length and last write time. Removable drives replace too. Where nothing can be replaced (the owner's policy), Replace is not offered: the user is asked before the copy, not refused after it, and a sync plan keeps such files (`f48d4a72`).
- **F-H3 and F-H9 (`4f6743e1`).** Only real links are links; OneDrive placeholders are folders and files. Below the folder the user chose, no link is followed; above it, links are followed as by any program, except by an elevated FileCat. macOS's `/var` and `/tmp` work again; elevated, only a link the system alone could have placed is followed.
- **F-H4 (`59cd42a9`).** SUBST paths stay inside the folder behind the drive.
- **F-H5 (`b685b782`).** The Registry import preview is linear in its input.
- **F-H6 and F-H7 (`f2ad9238`).** A page draws at most 200,000 table cells, and Markdown renders in linear time. That includes the security session's new FCSEC-042 and FCSEC-047.
- **F-H8 (`4f6743e1`).** A held folder made a mount point in place gets nothing.

**Also fixed:**
- **I560, Medium.** A destination held open without delete sharing is reported in use again, with Retry (an I22 regression).
- **`94501bb6`.** The comparison's one-sided review runs on its device worker.

**Hosted CI (I561).** The security session's `b42250a8` runs the Windows tests at medium integrity. `f77272e3` fixes what still failed:
- the WebView2 page tests run at the runner's own token;
- a restore-privilege test needs a high token;

- **Win11 VM, elevated:** the new link, SUBST, held-folder and Cloud Files tests pass. The 13 failures are six tests that are not elevation-aware, which hosted CI also failed at high integrity, and seven WebView2 tests without a desktop.
- **Mac and Ubuntu VM:** Core passes apart from tests that need a Git checkout or a `dotnet` host, which a copied build lacks; the network test that failed on the Mac is fixed. - **F-M1 (`e07f1156`).** An existing destination is reviewed only where it may be replaced. Skip and Keep, by policy or for all, read none, and a replaced file is read twice instead of three times. A question shown to the user still binds the file it shows.
- **F-M2 (`0ad1e951`).** Each side of a comparison has its own review budget, charged also for reviews that gave up. New items on one side can no longer leave the other side's unreviewed for Mirror to keep.
- **F-M7 (`ad19162c`).** NTFS recovery describes compressed files up to the volume's size, up to 2 million units, where 6.1 GiB per file was the limit.

Six Low of the recheck are fixed too. A rename answered with Replace replaces only the reviewed destination (C7). A bound replacement's renames are written through (C8). A ZIP's empty folder at the deepest level no longer blocks updates, and a ZIP whose names pass the budget lists its first entries (P6). mDNS names are charged the strings they become (P7). Elevated, a file beside checksum files says it was not checked, rather than looking like one nothing covers (P8). A replacement canceled after moving the original aside reports where the original is, and is journaled as partly applied (W9). Of the Codex review's Low, Git badges in a busy repository update again, and a snapshot closes a tip only when it changes a state (`a030d3d2`); FileCat's own Shift-drag moves, as F6 does, where it was refused as another app's (`04ca57ca`); the MTP device tests stop waiting after two minutes (`4c3940de`); a Linux page whose process ends or never starts says it is not shown (`2fb48cc1`); and tests now cross the FTP listing's line and wire limits (`e87b594f`). After that run, `da5e5734` closes a stopped SSH listing's folder on the server without making Stop wait for it; on the Mac, the old listing leaked the folder of every stopped listing until an sftp-server held to 64 descriptors failed, and the new one passes.

Locally at medium integrity, as hosted CI runs them, the four suites pass at `c448db09`: App 2,661 tests (81 skipped), Core 5,026 (167 skipped), Remote 2,664 (168 skipped) and the Windows platform suite 555 (42 skipped). The App fixes after it pass their own classes there, with the Git, browsing and viewer page tests; the new FTP limit tests pass against the owned server; and the MTP device tests skip with no phone connected. At high integrity, the elevated P8 test passes. On the Win11 VM, a folder handle that may add files flushes on FAT32, exFAT and NTFS, where one opened only to read is refused. The first build of this batch failed 2 Core, 32 Remote and 4 platform tests. The Remote ones expected a Move's check of its copy not to count as verification. Five found that reviewing only after the answer let a different file of the same size and time, put in place while the question waited, be replaced, or hid an identity error behind it; a shown question now reviews before it asks, and the review follows the backing-container check. One platform test, which times a registry preview, went over its 15 seconds while three suites ran together; it passes alone.

**Ledger.** Issues stay **561/540/2/19**, the evidence index **897**; the acceptance ledger has 33 Accepted and 12 Open. GATE-CI-FINAL stays Open for the run at `da5e5734`.

Stable publication remains NO-GO.
